subject: multiple R scripts "attached" to same session

messages.author: 54bc84ac59b7a4ae
messages.subject: multiple R scripts "attached" to same session
parts:
I'm a longtime vim user, and sporadic R user (through RStudio). It's very difficult for me to use RStudio's editor, but there are other features I like. One is that I can "attach" to the same workspace with different scripts.

So, with vim-r, what I want to do is attach multiple scripts to a single R session. That is:

1) open a script with vim
2) start R from inside vim
3) run a script to load data
4) close the script while keeping R workspace open
5) open a different script
6) attach to existing workspace with vim
7) do stuff with newly loaded script

Does this make sense? Is this possible?

Thanks!
ck

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: multiple R scripts "attached" to same session
parts:
If you close Vim and then restart it, it will set new values for environment variables used by Vim and R to recognize each other. So, you can't close Vim. (Please, see section "R must be started by Vim" of http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/r-plugin.html#r-plugin-known-bugs)

But without quiting Vim, you can :edit a new file and keep using Vim with different R scripts.

On Linux or Mac OS X, with Vim running in a terminal emulator in a Tmux session, if you press ^Az (or ^Bz if you haven't change Tmux scape command), Tmux will hide all panes and let only the current one visible. So, you can have either Vim or R full screen (press ^Az again to make all panes again).
